person: a cousin you grew up with
shape: an ordinary object that turns out to hold a whole memory

slides.text: you hid the [[dented biscuit tin]] behind grandma's water tank and swore it was full of stolen gold
so for three summers i guarded the path with a bamboo cane while the grown-ups talked inside
we sat on the back step splitting a bottle of warm orange squash, pretending we had a secret to protect
but on our last sunday before the long drive home, you pulled the tin out of the nettles and pushed it into my hands
there was no gold inside, just three smooth stones and a green plastic soldier with half a rifle missing
you said you made up the treasure [[so i wouldn't cry]] when my dad packed the suitcases into the boot
that little soldier is still on my desk, thirty years after grandma's house was sold

caption:
we spent two months of every year sharing bunk beds and drinking warm squash from plastic cups.
then the car boot slammed shut and we had to go back to different towns.
send this to the cousin who shared the fold-out couch with you every august.

#childhoodmemories #nostalgia #grandmashouse #growinguptogether
alt: a story about an old biscuit tin hidden behind grandma's house and the cousin who invented a treasure hunt to soften goodbye
